rows.en:
Alto's junior. An electronics whiz, he is also special adviser
to major firm L.A.I.'s tech research division. In battle he flies
the EW RVF-25, controlling drone fighters. (CV: Jun Fukuyama)

S.M.S. Pixie Team leader, flying a crimson Queadluun-Rhea.
In battle she's a giant Zentradi, but when micronized her body
turns into a little girl's. (CV: Megumi Toyoguchi)

S.M.S. Pixie Team leader. Micronized, a genetic anomaly
gives her a young girl's body, and oddly a childish personality.
Michel teases her; they always bicker. (CV: Megumi Toyoguchi)
An S.M.S. Skull Squadron pilot who serves as a medic when not in combat. A superb pilot, she flies the three-seat Konig Monster all by herself. (CV: Houko Kuwashima)
rows.notes: Canaria Berstein (female per glossary). Konig without umlaut (font).

rows.en: Helmsman of the Macross Quarter. He has a pure maiden's heart, but when he gets worked up in battle, rough macho talk may slip out... A maiden with a sweet crush on Ozma. (CV: Kenta Miyake)
rows.notes: Bobby Margot: male per glossary, speaks in feminine Japanese; the source calls him a maiden (otome), kept.

rows.en:
Captain of the Macross Quarter and the pillar of S.M.S.
A former pilot, reportedly as skilled as Ozma, with a broad
view that reads the tide of battle. (CV: Toru Okawa)

The Super Dimension Cinderella who met Alto & co. and ran up
the glorious stairway to idol stardom. Kira☆. Her love battle
with Sheryl over Alto has just begun. (CV: Megumi Nakajima)

A girl just starting up the stairway to idol stardom. Aiming for the top, she cosplays in all sorts of commercials. Apart from a song called "Aimo," her childhood memories are gone. (CV: Megumi Nakajima)
A diva hailed as the Galactic Fairy. Supremely confident in herself as Sheryl, she is extremely proud. Her love battle with Ranka over Alto has only just begun. (CV: Aya Endo)
A diva hailed as the Galactic Fairy. Close to Alto, whom she met on Frontier, she oddly knows the one song Ranka remembered, raising suspicion she's a Galaxy spy. (CV: Aya Endo)
rows.notes: 'Galaxy' = the Macross Galaxy fleet, as the Japanese says.

rows.en: Alto & co.'s classmate. A part-timer at Chinese diner Nyan-Nyan, she met Ranka there and feels more than friendship for her. Ranka Lee Fan Club founder and fan No. 1. (CV: Houko Kuwashima)

A cyborg pilot who blocked Alto time and again. Emotionless,
he saw his missions as his whole reason to exist, but through
his time with Ranka he slowly changes. (CV: Soichiro Hoshi)
No description for the Vajra.

Sheryl's formidable manager, but in truth the mastermind who
brought the Vajra to the Frontier fleet. She schemes to use the
power of Ranka and the Vajra to rule all. (CV: Kikuko Inoue)
An entertainment reporter for TV station SNN. Fighting the Mardook, he meets Silvie and Ishtar and awakens to a passion for bringing the truth to the people. (CV: Tsutomu Takayama)
Leader of the U.N. Forces' Faerie Squadron. A quarter Meltran, she inherited her grandmother's recklessness. She and Hibiki clash time and again, but slowly fall for each other. (CV: Yumi Toma)
rows.notes: Silvie Gena. 'Faerie Squadron' is a provisional glossary entry (the Japanese says Fairy Leader squadron).

rows.en:
An Emulator of the Mardook army. Taken by Hibiki, she met
Earth culture and learned what culture means. Through Ars's
song, she ended the Mardook war. (CV: Hiroko Kasahara)

Raised rich, he wanted for nothing, but bored of a life with no
thrills, he became a pilot. A seasoned veteran, foul-mouthed
but admired as a good big brother. (CV: Tetsu Inada)

Trained hard from childhood by her mercenary father, she's
a proven pilot. Perhaps as a single dad raised her, she's rough,
but has a feminine side: her hobby is cooking. (CV: Miho Hino)

A rookie who has dreamed of being a pilot since he was small.
Honest and earnest, with a slightly timid streak, but once his
blood is up, he shows a bold side. (CV: Jun Konno)

A passionate pilot who deeply loves the sky. His impulsiveness
lands him in all kinds of trouble, on and off the job. His hobby
is collecting oddly patterned T-shirts. (CV: Yuki Hayashi)

Born into a military family where all must serve, she became
a pilot, rare for a woman even there. Bright and friendly to all,
she often gives men the wrong idea. (CV: Hinako Sasaki)

An unlucky girl who enlisted hoping to be a mechanic, only to be made a pilot by her aptitude test. She is a quarter Zentradi, and her strong point is being full of pointless energy. (CV: Yoko Nishino)

rows.en:
EX-Gear Basics: Walk Mode
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.
rows.notes: Same three-line shape for every EX-Gear Basics header (u3551, u3559, u3564, u3567, u3574, u3575, u3582).

rows.en:
Push the analog stick down
to switch to Walk mode.

Press Up, Down, Left or Right on the D-pad
to move forward, back, left or right.
rows.notes: Same wording as the prefilled u3618 (same Japanese).

rows.en:
Quickly press the D-pad twice in the same
direction to step that way.
Keep holding the D-pad to dash.
Press the × button to jump.

Keep holding the × button mid-jump
to float in the air.

Press the D-pad while floating
to move through the air, too.
You can dash even in mid-jump.

Practice the Walk mode controls.
Leaving the room ends the training.

You can lock on to the red rings
by pressing the R button.

Press the L button to point the camera
in the direction of travel.

EX-Gear Basics: Hover Mode
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.

Push the analog stick left or right
to switch to Hover mode.

Press Left or Right on the D-pad to turn.
Press the L button to stop in place.

Quickly press the D-pad twice
in the same direction to step
that way.

At the end of a step,
keep holding the D-pad to dash.

Hold the × button to boost upward
and gain altitude.

Quickly press the × button twice
and keep holding it to boost
downward and lose altitude.

Practice the Hover mode controls.
Leaving the room ends the training.

EX-Gear Basics: Flight Mode
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.

Push the analog stick up
to switch to Flight mode.

Press Left or Right on the D-pad to turn,
Up to nose down and descend,
and Down to nose up and climb.

Press the × button
to boost and speed up.
rows.notes: Trailing newline kept as in the Japanese.

rows.en:
Practice the Flight mode controls.
Leaving the room ends the training.

EX-Gear Basics: Flight Mode
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.
rows.notes: Japanese writes EX-Gear without the hyphen here; same English.

rows.en:
Press the × button to boost.
Hold the △ button to brake
and slow down.

Quickly press Up, Left or Right on the D-pad
twice in the same direction to roll
that way.

EX-Gear Basics: Shooting Attacks
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.

Quickly press and release the R button
to lock on to an enemy.

While locked on, quickly press and release
the R button again to switch your lock
to another enemy.

Hold Up on the D-pad while locking on
to switch your lock to enemy warships
or enemy aces.

Press the □ button to shoot the target
you're locked on to.

While the locked-on target is in front of you,
your hit rate goes up.

Practice the shooting attack controls.
Leaving the room ends the training.

EX-Gear Basics: Shooting Attacks
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.

EX-Gear Basics: Melee Attacks & Guard
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.

In Walk and Hover modes, press
the △ button for melee attacks.

Press the △ button repeatedly
to chain melee attacks.

Lock on to a target. The
closer you are to it, the easier
it is to land melee attacks.

In Walk mode, hold
the L button to guard.
Guarding reduces the damage you take.

To dodge incoming balls,
use a step or a dash; to block them,
your best bet is to guard.

Practice the melee attack controls.
Leaving the room ends the training.

EX-Gear Basics: Melee Attacks & Guard
These instructions use the default
controller settings. Please keep this in mind.

Set a container down
near the start point to finish retrieving it.

You can also lift containers
in Hover mode.

Move close to a locked-on switch
to open the door.

Press the R button to lock on
to switches and containers.

EX-Gear mode names written 'Walk mode', 'Hover mode', 'Flight mode' (lowercase 'mode', like the prefilled 'Fighter mode' / 'Battroid mode' rows in slice 30); header lines capitalize them ('EX-Gear Basics: Walk Mode').
